report: A 72-year-old woman with behavioral change, falls and cognitive decline has CSF xanthochromia (4500 RBC/μL, protein 61), MRI T2* iron deposition in frontotemporal, insular, brainstem and spinal regions, arachnoiditis and spinal thecal siderosis, and no bleeding source on angioMRI; radiologist and laboratory physician confirm superficial siderosis from chronic SAH. Anticoagulation explains the chronic bleeding. This refutes pure FTD; NPH remains a treatable differential.
